subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Increasing the 'contrast' of a photo does what?
options: Makes darks darker and lights lighter
questions.explain: Increasing contrast widens the difference between the lightest and darkest tones.

questions.q: Crochet creates fabric using...
options: A single hooked needle to interlock loops
questions.explain: Crochet uses one hooked needle to pull yarn through loops, building up the fabric.

questions.q: A 'design brief' usually sets out...
options: The client's requirements and the target audience
questions.explain: A design brief defines the task, the client's needs and the intended target audience.

questions.q: A 'photogram' is made by...
options: Placing objects on light-sensitive paper and exposing it to light
questions.explain: A photogram is a cameraless image made by laying objects on photographic paper and exposing it to light.

questions.q: Corrugated card is useful in 3D work because it is...
options: Lightweight, strong and easy to score and fold
questions.explain: Corrugated card is light yet rigid, and can be scored and folded to build 3D forms.

questions.q: Why might a photographer use editing 'layers'?
options: To reduce the file to one flat image instantly
To stack and adjust separate elements independently
questions.explain: Layers let an editor stack and adjust separate elements without permanently altering the others.

questions.q: What is the key difference between shape and form?
options: Shape is large, form is small
Shape is two-dimensional, form is three-dimensional
Shape is coloured, form is not
questions.explain: A shape is flat and two-dimensional, while a form has depth and appears three-dimensional.

questions.q: What is cross-hatching?
options: Two sets of parallel lines crossing to build darker tone
Dotting the surface to suggest tone
questions.explain: Cross-hatching layers a second set of lines across the first to create darker, denser tone.

questions.q: 'Product design' is the discipline of...
options: Designing functional objects people use, such as appliances and furniture
questions.explain: Product design develops functional, manufactured objects, balancing how they work and look.

questions.q: Wool is a natural fibre obtained from...
questions.explain: Wool is a natural animal fibre sheared from the fleece of sheep.

questions.q: A 'mordant' is used in dyeing to...
options: Help the dye bond permanently to the fibre
questions.explain: A mordant fixes dye to the fibres so the colour is more permanent and less likely to wash out.

questions.q: Which genre focuses on capturing real events and everyday life truthfully?
questions.explain: Documentary photography records real events, people and life as honestly as possible.

questions.q: The rule of thirds suggests you place key features where?
options: In the exact centre of the image
Around the edges of the frame
Along lines that divide the image into thirds or at their intersections
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the picture into a 3x3 grid and places focal points on the lines or intersections.

questions.q: A slow shutter speed used on moving water typically creates...
questions.explain: A slow shutter speed records movement over time, smoothing flowing water into a soft blur.

questions.q: What is 'typography' in graphic design?
options: The art of arranging type and lettering
questions.explain: Typography is the design and arrangement of type so that text is legible and appealing.

questions.q: A 'relief' sculpture is one where...
options: Forms project from a flat background
questions.explain: In relief, the design is raised from (or sunk into) a flat background rather than standing free.

questions.q: Which artist is closely linked to Impressionism?
questions.explain: Claude Monet was a founder of Impressionism, famous for paintings such as his water lilies.

questions.q: What is a 'logo'?
options: A symbol or mark that identifies a brand
A full page of body text
questions.explain: A logo is a distinctive symbol or wordmark used to identify and represent a brand.

questions.q: A 'vector' image is one that...
options: Uses mathematical paths so it scales without losing quality
Is made of pixels and blurs when enlarged
Can only be black and white
questions.explain: Vector graphics use mathematical paths, so they can be scaled to any size without pixelation.

questions.q: What is 'slip' in pottery?
options: Liquid clay used to join pieces or decorate
questions.explain: Slip is clay mixed with water to a creamy liquid, used as a glue or for decoration.

questions.q: In one-point perspective, where do parallel lines appear to meet?
options: At a single vanishing point on the horizon
questions.explain: One-point perspective has receding lines converging at a single vanishing point on the horizon.

questions.q: What is a graphite pencil graded 'H' compared with one graded 'B'?
questions.explain: The 'H' scale denotes harder, paler pencils, while 'B' grades are softer and darker.
